literal: The remnant of the two called action and enmity, when considered, like the remnant of fire, will destroy.
translation: When one considers them, the unfinished remnants of an action or an enmity will destroy a person, just like a remnant of fire left unextinguished.
modern: செயல், பகை ஆகிய இரண்டின் எஞ்சிய பகுதி, ஆராய்ந்து பார்த்தால், அணையாமல் விடப்பட்ட நெருப்பின் எஞ்சிய பகுதி போல அழிவை உண்டாக்கும்.
explanation: This couplet warns against leaving any task or enmity incomplete. The poet compares the remnants of an unfinished action (வினை) and an unresolved enmity (பகை) to a spark of fire (தீ) that is not fully put out. Just as a tiny leftover ember can flare up and burn down an entire house, any unfinished portion of a task or a lingering trace of hostility will eventually grow and destroy the person who neglected it. Therefore, both work and enmity must be resolved completely without leaving any residue.
